title: Tech
dek: Desk, photo frame, audio and pocket tech picked from independent reviews, with the drawbacks included.

boards.title: The desk
boards.dek: Light, height and order for a desk setup, in wood and powder-coated steel.

boards.title: Digital photo frames
boards.dek: Engadget's top frames, none of which needs a subscription.

boards.title: Audio
boards.dek: A reviewer-favorite portable speaker and flagship noise-canceling headphones.

boards.title: Everyday carry
boards.dek: A tracker for your keys and a slim magnetic battery.

boards.title: The 256GB box
boards.dek: Used servers with 256GB of memory that run a 400B-class open AI model at home, from The Watch's build study; ask the seller how many DIMMs.

items.name: ScreenBar Halo 2 Monitor Light Bar
items.why: A monitor-mounted light bar with a wireless controller, presence detection and a rear backlight for the wall. How-To Geek measured about 1,000 lux at the center of the desk and called it one of the best options for ultrawide monitors; the main knock is the price.

items.name: Desk Shelf
items.why: A 9-inch-deep, 4.5-inch-tall monitor shelf in solid walnut, oak or maple, blackened walnut, or matte black or white. It comes in four widths from 18.5 to 58 inches.

items.name: Gather Compact Kit, Black/Maple
items.why: A powder-coated steel and maple desk system: a 26-inch monitor stand with built-in tray plus magnetic trays, a lid and a MagSafe phone stand you can rearrange. The Sweet Setup called Gather heirloom-quality and modular, with price the main drawback.

items.name: Carver Mat 10.1" Digital Frame
items.why: Engadget's best digital photo frame overall: a matted 10.1-inch screen with good color and little glare, app setup, unlimited cloud storage and no subscription. It can't be set up in portrait orientation.

items.name: Aspen Digital Frame
items.why: Engadget's honorable mention: an 11.8-inch, 1,600 x 1,200 display that works in portrait or landscape, with a physical control on the edge and no subscription. It costs more than the Carver.

items.name: 10" WiFi Digital Picture Frame
items.why: Engadget's budget pick: it loads photos from an SD card, USB drive, its app or Google Photos, turns to portrait or landscape and needs no subscription. The touchscreen picks up fingerprints and reflects more than the Aura.

items.name: Flip 7 Portable Speaker
items.why: What Hi-Fi?'s best portable Bluetooth speaker for 2026 (Award winner, five stars): smaller and cheaper than the Charge 6, with improved bass and an IP68 rating.

items.name: WH-1000XM6 Noise Canceling Headphones (open box)
items.why: Sony's current flagship over-ears, which TechRadar says improve on the XM5's sound and noise canceling and bring back the folding design. Battery life (30 hours with ANC) is ordinary and they are not water resistant; this open-box listing undercuts the $449 list price.

items.name: POP Bluetooth Tracker
items.why: A key-ring tracker that works with either Apple Find My or Google Find Hub, with a 120-decibel alarm. Tom's Guide found its range shorter than claimed (about 35 feet) and it has no ultra-wideband, but it suits mixed iPhone and Android households.

items.name: Nano Power Bank (5K, MagGo, Slim)
items.why: A 5,000 mAh Qi2 magnetic battery about 7.6 mm thick and 122 g, slim enough for a pocket. Pack Hacker scored it 7.9/10; it won't fully charge a large phone from empty and the glossy finish wears.
items.ebay: anker nano power bank 5k maggo slim

items.name: PowerEdge R630, 2× Xeon E5-2680 v4, 256GB (8 × 32GB)
items.why: The cheapest 256GB server in the build study: all four memory channels per socket lit, about 15 tok/s on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with a 12GB card. A 1U box, so the graphics card has to sit outside on a riser; stock isn't shown on the page.

items.name: PowerEdge R640, 2× Xeon Gold 6148, 256GB (16 × 16GB)
items.why: The study's reference platform: 16 sticks light all six channels on each socket, for 64 GB/s of usable bandwidth and about 4.6 tok/s on Qwen3.5-397B with 16k of context. Watch for the same title with 4 × 64GB, which runs at a third of the speed.

items.name: H12SSL-i + EPYC 7532 + 256GB DDR4-2666 (8 × 32GB)
items.why: A single-socket EPYC with all eight memory channels filled: 72 GB/s usable, 12% faster than the R640 for the same models. A bare board, so a case, power supply and SP3 cooler are extra; ask that the CPU is not vendor-locked.

items.name: H12SSL-i + EPYC 7532 combo (no memory)
items.why: Half of the study's fastest build under $5,000: add eight 32GB DDR4-3200 sticks for 87 GB/s, the most memory bandwidth you can buy used without moving to DDR5. Tested and working per the seller.
